facts.raw_span: a 3-year history of slowly progressive lower urinary tract symptoms
nocturia two to three times per night
a slow urinary stream
Urinalysis showed microscopic hematuria (3–5 red cells per high-power field)
no history of lichen sclerosis
no history of sexually transmitted infection
Renal ultrasonography findings were normal
Flexible cystourethroscopy revealed a circumferential urethral mass
biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma
biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition
Retrograde urethrography showed an approximately 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra
no palpable induration along the ventral penile shaft

concepts.why: The presence of a urethral mass with biopsy-proven amyloid protein deposition supports this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of slow urinary stream and the finding of a 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra support this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of slowly progressive lower urinary tract symptoms, including nocturia, support this diagnosis.
The presence of microscopic hematuria on urinalysis supports this diagnosis.
The finding of a circumferential urethral mass on flexible cystourethroscopy supports this diagnosis.
The biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma but demonstrated amyloid protein deposition, which is a characteristic finding in primary amyloidosis.

rationales.F04: Hematuria is a common symptom of many urological conditions, but its presence does not strongly rule in or out any of the listed concepts.
rationales.F08: A circumferential urethral mass is a significant finding that could be related to urethral amyloidosis or a urethral mass.
rationales.F09: The absence of carcinoma in the biopsy specimens rules out a urethral mass caused by carcinoma.
rationales.F10: The presence of amyloid protein deposition in the biopsy specimens strongly supports the diagnosis of urethral amyloidosis and also supports primary amyloidosis.
rationales.F11: The presence of a 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra strongly supports the diagnosis of urethral stenosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: Urethral Amyloidosis explains the urethral mass and amyloid protein deposition, with no strong contradictions, while Urethral Stenosis explains the slow urinary stream and stenosis in the penile urethra.
